relationships.subject: dexamethasone
relationships.evidence_quote: Saline-treated mice recovered within 2 weeks, whereas DEXA-treated mice experienced prolonged hyperalgesia for >10 weeks.

relationships.subject: diclofenac
relationships.evidence_quote: Similar to treatment with DEXA, mice treated with diclofenac developed long-lasting pain for more than 60 days after incision

relationships.subject: prostaglandin Gαs receptor agonists
relationships.evidence_quote: We observed that PG agonists prevented long-lasting DEXA-induced hyperalgesia in the DEXA-treated mice group

relationships.subject: prostaglandin Gαs receptor agonists
relationships.evidence_quote: plasma concentrations of S100A8/A9 at day 6 after incicion were significantly increased in DEXA-treated mice that received the PG agonist, treprostinil, compared to DEXA-only treated mice

relationships.subject: neutrophils
relationships.evidence_quote: We showed that the depletion of neutrophils abolished the protective effects of PG, indicating that these cells are required to prevent long-lasting pain.

relationships.subject: STAT3
relationships.evidence_quote: Stattic delayed the recovery of the mice treated with treprostinil

key_findings: DEXA or diclofenac after paw incision prolongs hyperalgesia for >60 days; prostaglandin Gαs agonists prevent and reverse it.
Effect requires neutrophils, S100A8/A9 and STAT3.
